'''Rubin Harold Landau''' (born 1944) is a Professor Emeritus of [[Oregon State University|Oregon State University's]] physics faculty, and a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]. 

== Early life and education ==
Rubin Harold Landau, the son of Philip and Bertha (Israel) Landau, was born in 1944 in [[New York City]]. He married Rebecca L. Kamelhar in 1965, and they had a daughter, Loretta. They divorced in 1984,<ref>{{Cite news |date=1984-07-24 |title=Dissolutions |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/corvallis-gazette-times-dissolutions/208987731/ |access-date=2026-10-25 |work=Corvallis Gazette-Times |pages=12}}</ref> and Landau married Janet Wilson Harris in 1986.<ref>{{Cite news |date=1986-07-14 |title=Marriage License Applications |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/statesman-journal-marriage-license-appli/209013407/ |access-date=2026-10-25 |work=Statesman Journal |pages=10}}</ref>

Landau earned his baccalaureate degree at [[Cornell University]] in 1965. His 1966 Master of Science, as well as his 1970 Doctor of Philosophy, were both from the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign|University of Illinois]].<ref name="Website-1">{{Cite web |title=Rubin H. Landau Papers, 1966-2008 |url=https://scarc.library.oregonstate.edu/findingaids/?p=collections/findingaid&id=2274 |access-date=2026-10-25 |website=scarc.library.oregonstate.edu |quote=From 1996 until his retirement in 2005, Landau had a joint appointment in the Physics and Computer Science Departments... Landau earned a BS from Cornell University in 1965 and graduate degrees from the University of Illinois in 1966 (MS) and 1970 (Ph.D.).}}</ref> His dissertation, titled ''Models for meson-deuteron scattering in the resonant region'', was advised by D.G. Ravenhall.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Landau |first=Rubin Harold |date=1970 |title=Models for meson-deuteron scattering in the resonant region |url=https://hdl.handle.net/2142/25857 |language=en}}</ref>

== Career ==
Landau held research associate positions at the [[University of Pittsburgh]] (1970–1972) and the [[University of British Columbia]] (1972–1974) before accepting a professorship at [[Oregon State University]] in 1974.<ref name="Website-1" /> Landau held joint appointments there in Physics and Computer Science Departments from 1996 to 2005.<ref name="Website-1" /> 

From 1974–1984 he was a visiting faculty member at the [[TRIUMF]] in Vancouver, Canada; and in 1977 at [[Lawrence Berkeley Laboratory]]. In 1980 he was a senior fellow at the [[University of Surrey]] in [[Guildford, England]]. Landau founded OSU's [[Computational physics|Computational Physics]] degree program, and has written more than 100 papers describing "computational studies of the scattering of elementary particles from subatomic systems," as well as "momentum space quantum mechanics."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Computational Problems for Physics by Rubin H Landau, Manuel José Pá |url=https://www.mcnallyrobinson.com/9781041166986/rubin-h-landau/computational-problems-for-physics |access-date=2026-10-25 |website=www.mcnallyrobinson.com |language=en}}</ref>

*1998 American Physical Society, Division of Computational Physics Fellowship, cited ''For innovative developments and practical applications of computational quantum physics to the scattering and exotic bound states of elementary particles, and for original books in quantum mechanics and computational physics.''<ref>{{Cite web |title=APS Fellows archive |url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship |access-date=2026-10-25 |website=www.aps.org |language=en}}</ref>
*2008 [[Krell Institute]] Undergraduate Computational Engineering and Sciences (UCES) Award<ref name="Jansen1">{{Cite news |last=Jansen |first=Henri |date=9 Nov 2009 |title=Letter From the Chair |url=https://physics.oregonstate.edu/sites/physics.oregonstate.edu/files/2022-10/Newsletter%202009.pdf |access-date=22 Oct 2026 |work=OSU Physics Newsletter |page=1}}</ref>
